scenes.title: REFORMING VIETNAM’S POLITICAL SYSTEM
scenes.subtitle: History of the Communist Party of Vietnam · Topic 6

beats.label: Our question
beats.heading: How can reform make the system work better for its people?
beats.body: Why reform · What changes · Our responsibility

notes: Good morning. Our topic is reforming Vietnam’s political system. We will use practical examples to explain why reform is necessary.
Our central question is simple: how can reform make Vietnam’s political system work better for its people? We will connect historical context, current changes and our responsibilities as students.

scenes.title: A system that serves people
scenes.subtitle: PART 01 · WHY REFORM?

beats.label: Leadership
beats.heading: Party leadership
beats.body: The Party leads the political system and is also part of it.

beats.label: Responsibilities
beats.heading: Different roles. Shared public purpose.
beats.body: The State manages public affairs under the law.

beats.label: People
beats.heading: The people’s mastery
beats.body: People are the focus of the system’s purpose.

notes: The textbook explains that the Party leads the political system and is also part of it. This is our starting point.
The State manages public affairs under the law. The Vietnam Fatherland Front and socio-political organisations also have distinct roles. These roles should remain clear when we discuss reform.
The people exercise their right to mastery. Reform therefore concerns how institutions organise work, coordinate and take responsibility. What happens when these connections become unclear?

scenes.title: Why reform becomes necessary
scenes.subtitle: A citizen’s journey · Illustrative model

beats.label: Enter
beats.heading: Where do I begin?
beats.body: One person. One application. Many connections.

beats.label: Tangle
beats.heading: Who takes responsibility?
beats.body: Overlapping steps can make a simple journey difficult.

beats.label: Apply Reform
beats.heading: Make the path clearer
beats.body: Clear responsibility. Better coordination.

beats.label: Economic change
beats.heading: Institutions must keep pace
beats.body: Development creates new demands.

beats.label: Effectiveness
beats.heading: Make responsibility clear
beats.body: Each task needs a lead and effective coordination.

beats.label: Integration
beats.heading: Build the capacity to adapt
beats.body: Clearer structures must work in practice.

notes: Imagine a person trying to submit one application. They see several offices and several possible routes. They need to know where to begin. This scene is an illustration of a problem, not a record of a real application.

The red cords represent overlapping procedures, crossing responsibilities and unclear coordination. They do not mean that the whole political system is chaotic. Notice the blocked route. If nobody takes the lead, the citizen may be asked to return or repeat information.

Let us apply reform. The cords separate and the routes become clearer. This shows the intended direction: clearer tasks and better coordination. The movement is a visual explanation. It is not evidence that a reform has already solved every problem.

Why is reform necessary? First, economic and social development creates new demands. Institutions need the capacity to respond. A structure that once worked may need to change as public needs and economic activity become more complex.

Second, administrative work needs clear responsibility. Resolution 18 calls for one agency to take the main responsibility for each task, while others coordinate. Fewer offices alone do not tell us whether an application becomes easier to complete. A clear lead also gives staff and citizens a place to ask for updates. Coordination remains necessary; the other offices still have duties.

Third, deeper international integration raises demands for capable and predictable institutions. These pressures make reform an ongoing task. After the pathways change, we still need to ask: can staff carry out their duties, and can people use the service?

scenes.title: Change has a history
scenes.subtitle: PART 02 · REFORM IN PRACTICE

beats.heading: 1986 · Đổi Mới
beats.body: Comprehensive renovation; renewed economic thinking.

beats.heading: 2017 · Organisational renewal
beats.body: Resolution 18: a streamlined, effective and efficient system.

beats.heading: 2025 · Local government reform
beats.body: Resolution 60: policy direction for restructuring.

notes: In 1986, the Sixth Congress responded to crisis with comprehensive Đổi Mới, or Renovation. It renewed economic thinking while keeping the socialist goal.
The process continued through Party renewal in 1992 and the 2011 Platform. In 2017, Resolution 18 focused on organisational structure, overlapping functions and responsibility.

In 2025, Resolution 60 provided direction for a specific local-government change. These milestones have different roles. They are not identical events or a simple chain that proves later reforms successful.

scenes.subtitle: RESTRUCTURING · A stylised model

beats.label: Before
beats.heading: 63 provincial-level units
beats.body: The starting structure.

beats.label: After
beats.heading: 34 provincial-level units
beats.body: What changed: the organisation of local government.

beats.label: Two tiers
beats.heading: Province → Commune
beats.body: Two-tier local government operating from 1 July 2025.

beats.label: Success
beats.heading: What determines success?
beats.body: A smaller structure must deliver in practice.

notes: Here is our main practical example. The model begins with 63 provincial-level units. Its shapes are stylised, so they should not be read as official administrative boundaries.

The move to 34 units is a verified organisational change. The policy aims to reduce administrative focal points and improve coordination. The animation makes the scale visible; it does not measure the quality of public services.

The Party Central Committee adopted Resolution 60 in April 2025. The National Assembly then adopted Resolution 202 and Law 72 in June. New local authorities began operating on 1 July, with province and commune levels. The district level ended. Commune-level units include communes, wards and special zones.

This gives us three layers: Party direction, a legal framework and implementation. Success depends on capable staff, clear duties, accountability and people’s experience. If citizens still submit the same papers in several places, changing the number of units is not enough. We need evidence about the actual service. A useful assessment asks about repeated submissions, access to help and clarity of responsibility, rather than relying on the new unit count alone.

scenes.title: NO EXCEPTIONS
scenes.subtitle: Policy principle

beats.label: Enforce
beats.heading: Enforce
beats.body: Address violations through the applicable rules.

beats.label: Prevent
beats.heading: Prevent
beats.body: Reduce opportunities for abuse.

beats.label: Disclose
beats.heading: Disclose
beats.body: Information needs verification and follow-up.

notes: Structure also needs integrity. The Political Report to the 14th National Party Congress calls for prevention and strict handling of violations, with no exceptions. This is a policy principle.

Prevention matters alongside enforcement. Clear duties, supervision and checks can reduce opportunities for abuse. The textbook’s lessons connect institution building with responsibility and control of power.

Decree 130 provides an example of asset and income control. Disclosure needs verification and follow-up. Our three labels summarise the discussion; they are not a quotation. Consistent implementation must be assessed through evidence.

scenes.title: The journey continues
scenes.subtitle: DIGITAL SERVICES · People at the centre

beats.label: Submit
beats.heading: Know where to submit
beats.body: Access online, with hands-on help when needed.

beats.label: Process
beats.heading: Know what happens next
beats.body: Reuse available data where permitted.

beats.label: Track
beats.heading: Know the status
beats.body: Follow progress and find support.

beats.label: Receive
beats.heading: Reach a clear outcome
beats.body: An accessible service keeps the whole journey visible.

notes: Our citizen returns. The first question is practical: where do I submit? An online portal helps only if people can use it. Hands-on support belongs inside the same service journey. The person who cannot use the portal should still have a practical route to complete the task.
Next comes processing. Reusing information where permitted can reduce repeated effort. The illustration does not claim a specific legal procedure or a guaranteed processing time.

People also need to follow progress and find help. Hanoi’s plan covers digital public-service skills across 126 communes and wards. The city has also called for mobile digital-literacy support. These are implementation measures, not proof that everyone has received assistance.

At the end, the person should know how to receive the result. The 2024 PAPI findings report gaps in digital access before the 2025 restructuring. They remind us to examine different people’s experiences. The lesson of taking the people as the root means asking whether residents can actually use the service.

scenes.title: What can students contribute?
scenes.subtitle: PART 03 · OUR RESPONSIBILITY

beats.label: Our role
beats.heading: What can students contribute?
beats.body: From understanding reform to taking responsibility.

notes: We have discussed institutions, responsibility and services. Our role as students begins with how we study these changes, work together and explain them honestly.

scenes.title: Responsibility starts with our work
scenes.subtitle: Topic 6 · Commitments to put into practice

beats.label: Learn deeply
beats.heading: Learn deeply
beats.body: Understand the argument. Check the original source.

beats.label: Participate
beats.heading: Participate
beats.body: Agree on tasks. Complete them. Support one another.

beats.label: Act with integrity
beats.heading: Act with integrity
beats.body: Separate verified facts, goals and interpretations.

notes: Academic responsibility means understanding the argument and checking the source. We should be able to explain why an example supports our conclusion.
Team responsibility means clear tasks, reliable work and support for others. Actual assignments remain for our members to confirm.

Presentation responsibility means answering with evidence and admitting what we do not know. We apply the textbook’s lessons about capability, people’s needs and practical implementation to our own learning.

scenes.title: Reform should improve people’s lives
scenes.subtitle: IMPLEMENTATION → GOALS → LONG-TERM VISION

beats.heading: 2025–26 · Implementation
beats.body: Structural changes are verified; service outcomes need evidence.

beats.heading: 2030 · Development goal
beats.body: Modern industry and upper-middle income.

beats.heading: 2045 · Long-term vision
beats.body: A developed, high-income country.

notes: The 2025–26 period concerns restructuring and implementation already under way. We distinguish verified changes from results that still need assessment.
For 2030, the development goal is modern industry and upper-middle income. Institutions are a means to support development. A future target is not an achieved result.

The 2045 vision is a developed, high-income country. The textbook’s lessons ask us to start from people’s needs and judge practical results. That connects our historical discussion to today. Let us now test these ideas together.

scenes.title: Đổi Mới 1986
scenes.subtitle: INTERACTIVE QUESTION 1

beats.label: Choose
beats.heading: Đổi Mới 1986
beats.body: Raise your hand for A, B, C or D.

notes: Read the question and allow time to think. Ask the class to raise their hands for A, B, C or D in turn. Select the class’s answer, then press Submit. Explain the reasoning briefly. Do not advance until the discussion is finished.

quiz.question: By the mid-1980s, Vietnam was in a socio-economic crisis under a centrally planned, subsidised economy. Which decision best matches the Party’s response at the Sixth National Congress in 1986?
options: Tighten central planning and subsidies to restore control over production.
Replace the socialist goal with a market model adopted from other countries.
Postpone economic changes until political institutions had been reorganised first.
Renew economic thinking and end the bureaucratic subsidy system, keeping the socialist goal.
quiz.explanation: The Sixth Congress, held in Hanoi on 15–18 December 1986, set out the line of comprehensive Đổi Mới. It called for renewing thinking, starting with economic thinking, and for ending the centrally planned, bureaucratic subsidy mechanism, and it is seen as a turning point in Vietnam’s transition to socialism. This is the starting point for later reforms of the political system; it does not show that any particular later reform has succeeded.

scenes.title: Restructuring
scenes.subtitle: INTERACTIVE QUESTION 2

beats.label: Choose
beats.heading: Restructuring
beats.body: Raise your hand for A, B, C or D.

notes: Read the question and allow time to think. Ask the class to raise their hands for A, B, C or D in turn. Select the class’s answer, then press Submit. Explain the reasoning briefly. Do not advance until the discussion is finished.

quiz.question: Which description matches the local government model that began operating on 1 July 2025?
options: 34 provincial-level units, with province and commune tiers.
63 provincial-level units, with province and commune tiers.
34 provincial-level units, with province, district, and commune tiers.
63 provincial-level units, with province, district, and commune tiers.
quiz.explanation: From 1 July 2025, local government has two tiers: province-level units (provinces and centrally run cities) and commune-level units (communes, wards and special zones), and the district level has ended. The model follows Party Central Committee Resolution 60-NQ/TW of 12 April 2025, and the National Assembly adopted Resolution 202/2025/QH15 on province-level units on 12 June 2025. This is an organizational change; whether services improve needs separate evidence.

scenes.title: People at the center
scenes.subtitle: INTERACTIVE QUESTION 3

beats.label: Choose
beats.heading: People at the center
beats.body: Raise your hand for A, B, C or D.

notes: Read the question and allow time to think. Ask the class to raise their hands for A, B, C or D in turn. Select the class’s answer, then press Submit. Explain the reasoning briefly. Do not advance until the discussion is finished.

quiz.question: The Sixth Congress (1986) put “take the people as the root” first among its main lessons. A commune offers online public services, but many older residents cannot complete the forms. Which action best applies this lesson?
options: Count the online applications received and treat the total as the measure of success.
Publish a written guide on the portal and ask residents to try again alone.
Provide hands-on help with submitting and show residents how to track progress.
Keep the online process unchanged and refer residents to relatives for help.
quiz.explanation: The Sixth Congress placed taking the people as the root first among its four main lessons, together with building and promoting the working people’s mastery. For public services, this means judging reform by whether residents can actually use and follow them. Hands-on help and progress tracking address the barrier directly; application counts, a written guide or a family referral do not show that it has been removed. A policy calling for such support does not establish that every resident has already received it.

scenes.title: One task, one lead
scenes.subtitle: INTERACTIVE QUESTION 4

beats.label: Choose
beats.heading: One task, one lead
beats.body: Raise your hand for A, B, C or D.

notes: Read the question and allow time to think. Ask the class to raise their hands for A, B, C or D in turn. Select the class’s answer, then press Submit. Explain the reasoning briefly. Do not advance until the discussion is finished.

quiz.question: Resolution 18-NQ/TW (2017) sets the principle that an agency may handle many tasks, but each task should have one lead agency with main responsibility. Three offices now review the same permit application, and each waits for the others. Which arrangement best follows this principle?
options: Keep the three reviews running in parallel and combine the opinions at the end.
Name one office as lead with main responsibility, and have the others coordinate through it.
Merge the three offices into one but keep the same three review steps.
Ask the applicant to coordinate between the offices and report any conflicts.
quiz.explanation: Resolution 18-NQ/TW (25 October 2017) of the 12th Central Committee calls for a political system that is streamlined and works effectively and efficiently; it names overlapping functions and weak accountability among the problems to solve. Merging offices, running reviews in parallel or passing coordination to citizens does not make responsibility clear. The example is illustrative and does not show how far overlap has been reduced in practice.

scenes.title: Thank you for listening
notes: We began with one question: how can reform help the system serve people better? A smaller structure is one step. Clear responsibility and accessible services must follow. Success depends on implementation and citizens’ experience. Our responsibility is to understand the evidence and explain it honestly. Thank you for listening.
